inputs.fx_note: Parity check 2026-09-26: MHJ.AX (ASX primary, AUD) closed 0.325; MHJ.NZ (NZX secondary, NZD) quoted 0.42. AUD/NZD spot (Yahoo AUDNZD=X) 1.2402 at time of check implies 0.325 x 1.2402 = NZ$0.4031 vs observed NZ$0.42 -- an ~4.2% premium on the thinly-traded NZX line, plausible for a micro-cap dual-listing with low NZX liquidity (ASX is the primary/deepest market). Statements and all flows are in AUD (financial statements filed in AUD); current_price and all *_iv fields are reported in the quote currency NZD per house convention, with an AUD-denominated twin (see *_aud fields) since AUD is the flows' native currency and the ASX line is far more liquid.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: 52/53-week year ending late June/early July (FY2026: 52 weeks to 28 June 2026)
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-currency WACC (flows are AUD). 10.5% reflects a cyclical discretionary retailer: unhedged gold/silver input cost exposure (no financial hedge on precious metals per FY26 risk note), a single-year turnaround unproven through a full economic cycle, and elevated leadership/governance transition (CEO death Feb-25, founder's passing Jul-25, new CFO Feb-26, Chair retiring Nov-26). This sits above a stable staples retailer (~8-9%) but below a pre-revenue or distressed name. Risk is charged once, in this single WACC across all three scenarios -- not stacked again as a per-scenario WACC premium, consistent with the cyclicality already being expressed via the scenario driver paths (section 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. Full lease payment (principal $47.965m FY26, from financing activities, PLUS interest $9.726m FY26, already inside operating cash flow as 'Leasing interest paid') is deducted from the flows via the engine's lease_cost_pct_path (FY26: 8.80% of revenue). Lease liabilities ($126.5m at FY26 year-end, dwarfing the $20.0m of actual bank borrowings) are EXCLUDED from net_debt/total_debt, which reflects borrowings only. D&A used for the cash-tax EBIT line is NON-ROU D&A only ($16.689m FY26 = total D&A $63.006m less right-of-use depreciation $46.317m; 2.55% of revenue) to avoid double-charging the lease (checklist item: EBIT for cash tax must be after D&A ex right-of-use depreciation). This ties to the company's own segment reporting, which already backs out AASB16 to derive 'Comparable EBIT' -- IFRS-16 lease liabilities are not debt-like (no cross-default, non-recourse to specific store leases) and including them in net_debt would swamp a $20m borrowings position with a $126m operating commitment.
inputs.nci_treatment: None required -- MHJ has no reported non-controlling interest; 100% Group-owned operations across Australia (incl. Bevilles), New Zealand and Canada. FY0 NOPAT ties to reported attributable net income without adjustment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Owner-FCF DCF (component build), 10-year horizon, routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md as a non-US, cyclical operating retailer, using owner-fcf.md plus the owner-fcf-adaptations.md (currency mismatch, lease treatment B, SBC-zero market). FRESH BUILD (no prior DCF/Drivers file existed). KEY JUDGMENT -- MID-CYCLE MARGIN: FY2026 was a genuine but single-year turnaround (Comparable EBIT margin 3.67%, up from a FY2024/25 trough of ~2.4%, but still far below the FY2022/23 pre-trough level of ~9.4-10.6% and the company's own stated 10% medium-term ambition). The component build does NOT extrapolate FY26's improving trajectory to the 10% target (unproven over a full cycle per the Analysis JSON bear case -- Bevilles and NZ recoveries are each less than a year old, no gold/silver hedging exists, and there has been unusually high leadership churn). Base case reaches only ~6.1% EBIT margin by year 10 (roughly the midpoint between FY26 delivery and management's ambition); bull reaches ~10.1% (full ambition delivered, Canada rollout to 85-90 stores completes on schedule); bear stalls near ~2.2% (close to the FY24/25 trough, consumer downturn plus unmitigated gold-cost pressure). CASH TAX: FY26's disclosed effective tax rate of 43.5% is distorted by a one-off $7.5m Australian tax refund landing on a low pretax profit base (income tax RECEIVED, not paid, per the FY26 cash flow statement: +$0.324m net inflow); ramped down to a blended AU/NZ/Canada statutory run-rate of ~28-29% by year 3, consistent with the pre-distortion FY22/23 effective rates of 28.9%/29.3%. WORKING CAPITAL: wc_capture_pct set modestly negative (manufacturer/retailer carrying high-value gold/diamond inventory; FY26's net-debt reduction was partly funded by a one-off $9.4m inventory drawdown that must reverse as the business grows, only partially offset by the PCP deferred-revenue tailwind). CAPEX: FY27 guided to ~$25m (from $14.2m FY26) for Canada store rollout/SaaS; modelled as an elevated near-term capex_pct_path (3.6% of revenue year 1) tapering back to a ~2.2-2.3% maintenance level once the rollout completes. SBC: immaterial/near-zero (Australian/NZ/Canadian retailer, not a US tech comp) -- SBC-zero-market treatment per adaptations section (e): rows kept explicit at 0% rather than deleted; band_position set to null since house and street coincide. TERMINAL CAP: 12x reflects a cyclical, historically low-multiple retailer -- FY26 year-end EV/Comparable-EBIT was only ~5.5x, indicating the market is currently pricing in material doubt about the turnaround's durability; 12x on owner FCF is a moderate, not generous, assumption for a matured, de-levered version of this business.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-2.2% to -2.8%) is materially negative while revenue grew modestly (+1.4% to +3.3%) -- a >30% divergence. This is explained, not anomalous: FY2024 posted a near-breakeven statutory loss (-$0.479m) after a multi-year EBIT-margin collapse from ~13% (FY21) to 2.2% (FY24), compounded by a $7.4m Bevilles brand impairment in FY25 and $30.7m/$20.2m of dividends paid in FY23/FY24 against thin underlying earnings -- i.e. equity was drawn down by real trading weakness and shareholder distributions during the trough, not by an accounting artefact. EPS and reported-FCF CAGRs are not used as the growth anchor: EPS swung from 9.0c (FY23) through a loss (FY24) to 2.5c (FY26), and reported FCF is structurally inflated by IFRS-16 (owner FCF, net of the full lease payment, was actually NEGATIVE in FY24 and FY25 -- see notes on owner_fcf history below), so neither series is a usable CAGR base. Revenue 5yr CAGR (3.3%) is used as the growth anchor because it is the only series not distorted by the margin cycle; the margin recovery itself is modelled explicitly via the component EBIT-margin path (mid-cycle judgment), not via the growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF history (reported_fcf less lease principal, SBC and interest income) is materially negative to slightly positive across the cycle: FY2024 -$39.6m, FY2025 -$3.7m, FY2026 +$36.7m -- confirming that reported FCF (which nets IFRS-16 lease interest but not lease principal) substantially overstated true free cash flow in the trough years. This is why a component margin build (not a flat historical FCF multiple or a reported-FCF CAGR) is essential for this ticker.

base.narrative: The operational reset (CEO Waecker, from Aug-2025) continues to deliver, but only partially closes the gap to management's own 10% medium-term EBIT margin ambition -- Canada's store rollout (81 -> 85-90) and continued Brilliance/PCP/digital penetration lift EBIT margin from FY26's 3.0% (component-build basis) to ~6.1% by year 10, roughly the midpoint of FY26 delivery and the stated target, reflecting genuine but incomplete execution against a still-untested full economic cycle. Growth decelerates from the FY26 constant-currency run-rate (~4.1%) toward a 2.5% terminal rate as store-count growth slows and Canada matures. Cash tax normalizes from FY26's refund-distorted 43.5% to a ~29% blended AU/NZ/Canada run-rate by year 3.

bull.narrative: Management's 10% medium-term EBIT margin ambition is substantially delivered (reaching ~10.1% by year 10): Canada completes its 85-90 store build-out with sustained high-teens same-store-sales growth and its already-best-in-group 12.6% segment margin extends further, Bevilles' H2-FY26 recovery (+5.8% same-store sales) proves durable through a full cycle, gross margin resilience (60.5%, defended through record gold prices) continues without a hedging program becoming necessary, and the newly-disclosed $57m PCP deferred-revenue book converts smoothly into high-margin recognised revenue. Digital penetration (8.7% of FY26 revenue, below peers per management's own framing) closes the gap faster than base case, supporting sustained mid-single-digit growth for longer before decelerating.

bear.narrative: The FY26 turnaround stalls or partially reverses: a consumer discretionary downturn (cost-of-living pressure, weaker household budgets across AU/NZ/Canada) hits same-store sales just as further gold/silver price records outpace the company's ability to reprice without demand destruction (no financial hedge exists), compressing gross margin. Bevilles' H2-FY26 recovery and New Zealand's stabilisation prove to be one-off halves rather than a trend, the newly-disclosed PCP revenue stream sees further negative assumption revisions (as already happened in H2 FY26, a $4.6m headwind), and the elevated cadence of leadership/board transition (new Chair Nov-2026, on top of the CEO/founder/CFO changes since 2025) disrupts execution momentum. EBIT margin regresses toward the FY24/25 trough (~2.2% by year 10) and stays there; capex is cut back toward maintenance levels as the Canada rollout is paused.

scenario_narratives.base: Partial, credible progress against management's own 10% EBIT margin ambition -- FY26's real but single-year turnaround continues at a measured pace, reaching roughly 6% EBIT margin by year 10 as Canada's rollout and PCP/digital growth offset only some of the structural thinness of jewellery retail margins.
scenario_narratives.bull: Management's turnaround thesis plays out close to plan: Canada's 85-90 store target is reached with sustained high growth and margin, Bevilles' recovery holds through a full cycle, and the 10% medium-term EBIT margin ambition is essentially delivered.
scenario_narratives.bear: A consumer downturn meets unmitigated (unhedged) gold-price inflation just as the FY26 recovery is tested for the first time through a full cycle; Bevilles/NZ recoveries prove to be one-off halves, PCP assumptions move against the company again, and leadership churn (new Chair Nov-2026) disrupts execution -- EBIT margin regresses toward the FY24/25 trough.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised above the 15% house default to 30% because the bull/base cases both require a single strong year (FY26) to be the start of a genuine multi-year structural improvement rather than a cyclical bounce off a very depressed FY24/25 base -- the company's own Chair's letter describes the business as still at 'the early stages of our business reset', Bevilles and New Zealand each have less than one full year of demonstrated recovery, there is no financial hedge against further record gold/silver prices, and the business has an unusually high recent cadence of leadership/governance transition (CEO death, founder's passing, new CFO, and now a Chair handover within about 20 months). Bull weight trimmed to 25% because it requires several largely independent things to go right simultaneously (Canada store rollout on schedule, Bevilles proving durable, PCP recognition not reversing again, gross margin holding without a hedge) rather than one dominant driver. Base weight of 45% (below the 50% default) reflects that this is a genuine turnaround story still resting on one audited year of proof.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Michael Hill is a specialty jewellery retailer emerging from a multi-year margin collapse (EBIT margin fell from ~13% in FY2021 to a 2.2% trough in FY2024) with a genuine but single-year (FY2026) recovery: Comparable EBIT margin improved to 3.67% (still far below the FY22/23 pre-trough level of ~9-11% and management's own stated 10% medium-term ambition), net debt was cut from $41.9m to $5.5m, and a dividend was resumed after a two-year suspension. The valuation is built on owner FCF net of the FULL IFRS-16 lease cost (principal, which sits in financing activities and is NOT captured in reported FCF, plus interest, which is already inside reported operating cash flow) -- this is a large and consequential adjustment: owner FCF was actually negative in FY2024 (-$39.6m) and FY2025 (-$3.7m) once the true lease cost is deducted, only turning solidly positive in FY2026 (+$36.7m, a 5.6% owner-FCF margin versus the 13% reported-FCF margin). A mid-cycle margin judgment is used rather than extrapolating FY26's improving trajectory to management's 10% target: base case reaches only ~6.1% EBIT margin by year 10. Given the market is currently pricing the stock at only ~5.5x EV/Comparable-EBIT, a wide bear/bull spread and an above-default 30% bear weight are appropriate -- the market itself appears skeptical that FY26 is the start of a durable structural improvement rather than a cyclical bounce.
key_risks_to_valuation: FY2026's recovery is one audited year deep; Bevilles and New Zealand's positive same-store-sales trends are each less than a full year old
No financial hedging program exists for gold/silver, the single largest identified cost pressure, after prices have 'nearly doubled' over two years per the outgoing Chair
PCP (extended-warranty) revenue recognition is a Key Audit Matter subject to material assumption risk -- a $4.6m negative swing already occurred in H2 FY26

Elevated leadership/governance transition cadence (CEO's sudden death, founder's passing, new CFO, and a Chair handover effective Nov-2026 within ~20 months) creates execution continuity risk right as the turnaround needs sustained focus

Lease treatment materially changes the picture: excluding the $126.5m of lease liabilities from net debt (treatment B) is the correct basis given they are not recourse debt, but a reader applying treatment A (leases as debt) to the same cash flows would derive a very different net-debt bridge -- the two must never be mixed
FY2027 capex step-up to ~$25m for the Canada rollout will pressure free cash flow if same-store-sales momentum stalls before the higher store base matures
